findings.title: Entire /api/v1/security/* router is unauthenticated (14 endpoints, 4 of them SIEM writes)
evidence: No Depends(...) anywhere in app/api/security.py
Runtime: all 10 GET endpoints returned HTTP 200 with no Authorization header
Control in same run: GET /api/v1/todos/ -> 403, GET /api/v1/users/me -> 403
Runtime: POST /simulate/powershell with user='DOMAIN\\Administrator', host='dc01.corp.local', source_ip='203.0.113.9' -> 200 {'status':'success'}
findings.impact: Anonymous read of raw SIEM telemetry (IPs, usernames, hostnames, command lines) and anonymous write of forged security events that the detectors consume as ground truth. Also an unauthenticated DoS/alert-spam amplifier via /threats/scan BackgroundTasks and the unbounded hosts list.
findings.expected_behavior: Authentication required; simulation endpoints gated by role and non-production environment.
findings.validation: Live HTTP probe against uvicorn on 127.0.0.1:8099; 403 control endpoints prove the gap is router-specific.
findings.recommended_fix: Add dependencies=[Depends(get_current_active_user)] at app/main.py:47; gate /simulate/* by role + settings.environment; bound LateralMovementSimulation.hosts.
findings.documentation_impact: docs/API_DOCUMENTATION.md:351 claims all endpoints except register/login require JWT - false. The 4 /simulate/* write endpoints are undocumented entirely.

findings.title: JWT signing key and passwords committed to a public repository
evidence: kind: Secret with base64 SECRET_KEY, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, ELASTIC_PASSWORD, KIBANA_PASSWORD
git ls-files confirms tracked; first committed in 2bdbbba; repository is public
gitleaks independently flagged generic-api-key and kubernetes-secret-yaml at this file
app-secrets is consumed by backend.yaml and migrate-job.yaml (reachability confirmed)
configmap.yaml:16 places a plaintext DATABASE_URL with password in a ConfigMap
findings.impact: Anyone can forge a valid HS256 JWT for any user against any Kubernetes deployment using these manifests. ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES here is 43200 (30 days) and no revocation mechanism exists.
findings.expected_behavior: Secrets sourced from a secret manager, never committed.
findings.validation: Static: file tracked in git, decodes to a 48-byte key, wired into the backend Deployment env.
findings.recommended_fix: Rotate the key immediately; remove the Secret from git; use sealed/external secrets; purge from history.
findings.documentation_impact: docs/KUBERNETES_DEPLOYMENT.md:166 refers to a Secret without warning that it is committed with real values.

findings.title: Password-reset OTP is non-cryptographic and brute-forceable; full account takeover
evidence: email_service.py:16 uses random.choices (MT19937), not secrets; secrets is never imported
PoC: OTP sequence fully reproducible from generator state; state recoverable from 624 outputs
Runtime: 60 consecutive wrong OTPs -> 60 x HTTP 400, no 429, no lockout
Runtime: 50 consecutive failed logins -> 50 x HTTP 401, no 429
grep for ratelimit|slowapi|limiter across app/ returns nothing
Runtime: 5 forgot-password calls produced 5 simultaneously valid unused OTPs
Measured 66.7 req/s sequential on loopback; 10^6 keyspace exhaustible within the 15-minute OTP window at modest concurrency
findings.impact: Account takeover of any account whose email is known.
findings.actual_behavior: 6-digit MT19937 OTP, 15-minute window, unlimited guesses, multiple OTPs valid at once, stored in cleartext.
findings.expected_behavior: CSPRNG token, single valid OTP, attempt limiting with lockout, hashed storage.
findings.validation: Live scripted brute force plus an offline generator PoC. Single-use and owner-scoping were separately verified as working correctly, bounding the finding.
findings.recommended_fix: secrets.choice; longer/alphanumeric token; per-account attempt counter and lockout; invalidate prior OTPs on issue; throttle forgot-password; store a hash.
findings.documentation_impact: Password-reset semantics are undocumented entirely (gap G5).

findings.title: Threat detection fails open: Elasticsearch 401s are swallowed and reported as 'no threats'
evidence: threat_detection.py:11 builds Elasticsearch([...]) with no credentials; security_logger.py:16 uses basic_auth
Runtime against a security-enabled ES 8.11.0: write path succeeded, index security-powershell-logs-2026.10.07 created
Runtime: GET /threats/brute-force -> 200 {'threats':[],'count':0}
Server log: AuthenticationException(401, 'security_exception', 'missing authentication credentials for REST request [/security-*/_search]')
All 8 detectors catch broadly and return []
findings.impact: The product's core capability is inoperative whenever Elasticsearch security is enabled - which is the shipped docker-compose configuration. A broken detector is indistinguishable from a clean result, so an operator sees '0 threats' and concludes they are safe.
findings.actual_behavior: Detectors return HTTP 200 with an empty list while every query 401s.
findings.expected_behavior: Authenticated queries; failures surfaced as 503/degraded, never as an empty result.
findings.validation: Reproduced end to end against a real security-enabled Elasticsearch, with the authenticated writer path working in the same run as a control.
findings.recommended_fix: Share one authenticated ES client factory; re-raise or return an explicit degraded status instead of [].
findings.documentation_impact: Invalidates the 'WORKING' rule claims in docs/KIBANA_ESQL_ALERTING_RULES.md:60 and all efficacy metrics in SECURITY.md:314-318.

findings.title: docker-compose.yml is invalid YAML; the documented setup cannot start
evidence: docker compose up -d -> failed to parse docker-compose.yml: line 284: mapping key 'depends_on' already defined at line 266
Present in HEAD commit 88746ef, not only the working tree
Removing the second depends_on in a scratch copy makes the file parse cleanly (exit 0), so it is the only YAML blocker
findings.impact: No one cloning the repository can start the stack. docker compose up -d is the primary documented quick-start in five separate documents.
findings.validation: docker compose config and docker compose up --dry-run both fail; verified fixed in an isolated copy.
findings.recommended_fix: Delete docker-compose.yml:284-285 and merge logstash into the depends_on block at :266; add docker compose config to CI.
findings.documentation_impact: README.md:55, docs/index.md:45, SECURITY.md:234, docs/SETUP_AND_TROUBLESHOOTING.md:151 and CLAUDE.md all document a command that fails.

findings.title: elastic123 hardcoded as cluster superuser password repository-wide
evidence: gitleaks: 71 curl-auth-user hits across docs and scripts
No ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD key exists in .env, so the config.py:18 default is what actually runs
findings.impact: A single published password grants elastic superuser on every default deployment.
findings.recommended_fix: Source from a secret store with no default; fail closed when unset; rotate; purge from docs.
findings.validation: Static inspection; see FINDINGS.md for detail.

findings.title: Live .env secrets and an RSA private key are baked into the backend image; container runs as root
evidence: .dockerignore omits .env, *.pem and test.db; Dockerfile:12 is COPY . .
No USER directive; gcc retained in the final layer
.env holds a live-format Slack webhook, a Gmail app password, an OTX API key, SECRET_KEY and KIBANA_SYSTEM_PASSWORD
Verified: .env and sentinel.pem were never committed to git
findings.impact: Anyone able to pull the image reads all five secrets plus an unencrypted RSA private key.
findings.recommended_fix: Add .env, *.pem, test.db to .dockerignore; add a non-root USER; multi-stage build; rotate the secrets.
findings.validation: Static inspection; see FINDINGS.md for detail.

findings.title: JWT stored in a JavaScript-readable cookie for 30 days
evidence: httpOnly: false with the comment 'Allow client-side access'
Secure omitted when protocol is not https
middleware.ts checks cookie presence only - any string passes
findings.impact: Any XSS yields full account takeover for 30 days; token crosses the wire in cleartext given nginx is HTTP-only.
findings.recommended_fix: httpOnly cookies with a server-side exchange; Secure always; shorter lifetime; add CSP.
findings.validation: Static inspection; see FINDINGS.md for detail.

findings.title: User enumeration oracle on /forgot-password
evidence: Runtime with SMTP unreachable: existing email -> HTTP 500, unknown email -> HTTP 200
Contradicts the code's own comment at users.py:89

findings.validation: Static inspection; see FINDINGS.md for detail.

findings.title: Elasticsearch and Kibana are unauthenticated in all Kubernetes manifests
evidence: xpack.security.enabled set to 'false' in both manifests
ingress.yaml defines a kibana-loadbalancer with no tls: block and ssl-redirect disabled
Note: ingress.yaml is excluded from kustomization.yaml:18, so the LoadBalancer is not applied by default
findings.impact: Anyone reaching the service reads and writes all security indices and Kibana saved objects.
findings.recommended_fix: Enable xpack security in k8s; add NetworkPolicies; authenticate Kibana; add TLS.
findings.validation: Static inspection; see FINDINGS.md for detail.

findings.title: Packetbeat captures full HTTP request and response bodies including credentials
evidence: send_request: true and send_response: true for ports [80,8080,8002,5000,9200]
Output to Logstash with no credentials and no TLS
findings.impact: Login bodies (username+password), Authorization headers and reset OTPs are captured verbatim and indexed, turning the monitoring layer into a plaintext credential store.
findings.recommended_fix: Disable body capture; exclude the application's own ports; redact headers; enable TLS and auth on the output.
findings.validation: Static inspection; see FINDINGS.md for detail.

findings.title: No TLS anywhere in the shipped topology
evidence: nginx listens on 80 only - no ssl_certificate, no 443 server, no redirect, no HSTS
ES http and transport SSL disabled
Logstash inputs have no ssl_enabled
next.config.mjs:36 sends HSTS the server cannot honour
findings.impact: JWTs, passwords, OTPs, elastic123 and all telemetry cross every hop in cleartext.
findings.recommended_fix: Terminate TLS at nginx/ALB; redirect 80->443; enable TLS on ES, Logstash and beats.
findings.validation: Static inspection; see FINDINGS.md for detail.

findings.title: Security alerting is a hardcoded placeholder; alerts reach nobody
evidence: Webhook defaults to https://hooks.slack.com/services/YOUR/SLACK/WEBHOOK and the only caller passes one argument

send_email_alert builds a MIMEText and never sends it

findings.title: No application rate limiting; nginx auth_limit declared but never applied
evidence: Only api_limit is applied, to /backend/; auth_limit and general_limit are referenced by no location
Runtime: 50 logins + 60 OTP guesses produced zero 429s
docker-compose publishes the backend on 0.0.0.0:8000, bypassing nginx entirely

findings.title: 50 known vulnerabilities across 9 Python dependencies; multipart DoS reachable pre-auth

python-multipart 0.0.6 (8 advisories) and starlette 0.27.0 (10) parse the unauthenticated login form at app/api/users.py:41
python-jose 3.3.0 PYSEC-2024-233 reachable on every authenticated request
Triaged NOT exploitable: PYSEC-2024-232 algorithm confusion - auth.py:36 pins algorithms; ecdsa - HS256 only

findings.title: npm ci fails; production build is not reproducible

Dockerfile uses npm i -f, overriding peer resolution and shipping vaul against an unsupported React major
Four dependencies pinned to the floating tag 'latest'

findings.title: Password change does not invalidate existing JWTs
evidence: Runtime: token issued, password changed in DB, same token still returned 200 on /users/me
findings.impact: A stolen token survives a password reset; 30 min in .env, 30 days in k8s.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a token version or password_changed_at claim; add logout and a denylist.

findings.title: Login timing oracle enables account enumeration
evidence: Returns at :46 for an unknown user without performing any bcrypt work
findings.impact: Response-time difference of a full bcrypt cost-12 computation distinguishes existing accounts.
findings.recommended_fix: Always compare against a dummy hash.

findings.title: /health returns 200 when unhealthy and leaks a DB connection per probe
evidence: Runtime with Redis down: HTTP/1.1 200 OK body {'status':'unhealthy','database':'ok','redis':'error'}
engine.connect() is never closed and is not a context manager
findings.impact: Kubernetes probes can never fail, so a broken pod is never restarted - while the same endpoint exhausts the connection pool.
findings.recommended_fix: Return 503 when unhealthy; use with engine.connect().

findings.title: Todo statistics cache is never invalidated
evidence: Runtime with live Redis: stats reported total_todos=1 after a create while GET /todos/ returned 2 items
findings.impact: Users see stale statistics for up to 120 seconds.
findings.recommended_fix: Delete stats:user:{id} in create/update/delete.

findings.title: Validation errors echo rejected values to the client and to Elasticsearch
evidence: Runtime: POST /users/reset-password with non-string otp/new_password returned and logged 'input': 123456 and 'input': 55512345

SCOPE CORRECTED: the broader claim that any validation failure leaks the password was tested and DISPROVED - input is per-field and password/otp are unconstrained str, so only type-validation failures leak
findings.impact: Secret-bearing values reach the SIEM and the client on malformed input.
findings.recommended_fix: Strip input/ctx from logged and returned payloads; add a structlog redaction processor.

findings.title: SMTP TLS unverified and untimed; blocking call in an async path; HTML injection into email
evidence: starttls() without an SSL context - no certificate verification
smtplib.SMTP constructed without a timeout
user.username f-string-interpolated unescaped into HTML email
Errors print() to stdout, bypassing the log pipeline
findings.impact: MITM of the mail session can capture the Gmail app password; a hung SMTP server blocks the entire event loop indefinitely.
findings.recommended_fix: ssl.create_default_context(); explicit timeout; background queue; escape template values.

findings.title: Alembic migration is Postgres-only and is never exercised by tests
evidence: alembic upgrade head against SQLite fails: server_default=func.now() emits DEFAULT now()
Tests use Base.metadata.create_all, so they validate models and never the migration
Model-vs-migration comparison showed no drift today
env.py sets neither compare_type nor compare_server_default
findings.impact: The migration could break entirely and the test suite would stay green.
findings.recommended_fix: Run migrations against Postgres in CI and assert the schema matches the models.

findings.title: Blocking synchronous I/O throughout async handlers
evidence: Sync redis, elasticsearch, requests and smtplib clients all called inside async def
smtplib.SMTP has no timeout, so /forgot-password can stall the event loop indefinitely
findings.impact: Concurrent requests serialise behind every external call; one hung SMTP connection stalls the whole process.
findings.recommended_fix: redis.asyncio, AsyncElasticsearch, httpx.AsyncClient; background queue for SMTP; explicit timeouts.

findings.title: Redis KEYS used for cache invalidation on every write; unbounded key growth from user input
evidence: KEYS is O(N) and blocks the Redis server; called on every todo create/update/delete
The raw search parameter is interpolated into the cache key with no bound
findings.impact: Redis-wide latency spikes; a memory-exhaustion path via arbitrary search strings.
findings.recommended_fix: Use SCAN or a per-user key set; hash the filter component of the key.

findings.title: /metrics is unauthenticated with unbounded Prometheus label cardinality
evidence: Runtime: GET /metrics -> 200 with no auth
endpoint label uses the raw request path, so every todo id creates a new time series
findings.impact: Operational intelligence disclosure plus an anonymous memory-exhaustion vector.
findings.recommended_fix: Authenticate or bind internally; label by route template.

findings.title: Logstash mounts a developer's absolute hostPath; the pod cannot start
evidence: hostPath /home/rcsen/Documents/sih25/ps25238/logstash/pipeline with type: Directory - a path that does not match this repository's name
PVs use hostPath under /tmp with Retain
findings.impact: Logstash will not schedule on any other node; persistent data is node-local and lost to /tmp cleanup.
findings.recommended_fix: Ship the pipeline as a ConfigMap; use real StorageClasses.

findings.title: Privileged and root containers, host networking, cluster-wide RBAC, no securityContexts
evidence: privileged: true initContainer; beats DaemonSets runAsUser 0 with hostNetwork: true and cluster-wide get/list/watch
No securityContext at all on postgres, redis, logstash, kibana, backend, frontend or migrate-job
No PodSecurity admission and no NetworkPolicy anywhere in the tree
findings.impact: Compromise of either beats DaemonSet yields root on the host network with cluster-wide read.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop privileged; add restrictive securityContexts; scope RBAC; add NetworkPolicies.

findings.title: 13 service ports published on 0.0.0.0 including password-less Redis and Postgres
evidence: docker compose config resolves published ports 80,514,3000,5000,5044,5432,5601,6379,8000,9200,9300,9600,12201 with no host_ip binding
Redis is started with no requirepass
findings.impact: Direct network access to the database, cache and search cluster, and complete bypass of nginx rate limiting and routing.
findings.recommended_fix: Bind to 127.0.0.1 except nginx; set a Redis password.

findings.title: Conflicting CORS policy between nginx and the application
evidence: App allows hardcoded localhost origins with allow_credentials=True; nginx adds Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on /backend/
findings.impact: Browsers reject wildcard origin with credentials; duplicate headers are a protocol error. Deployed origins never match the hardcoded list.
findings.recommended_fix: Drive origins from configuration; set CORS headers in exactly one layer.

findings.title: pytest.ini uses [tool:pytest] and is silently inert

Verified: pytest reports configfile: pytest.ini but addopts = -v --tb=short does not take effect
findings.impact: Any future --cov-fail-under or --strict-markers would be ignored silently.
findings.recommended_fix: Rename the section to [pytest].

findings.title: TypeScript and ESLint errors suppressed at build time; 13 errors hidden
evidence: tsc --noEmit reports 13 errors; 3 are genuine type-safety failures where apiCall is called without a type parameter so T widens to {}
strict is false across 9089 LOC
findings.impact: state.todos.map() would throw if the API returned a non-array; there is no runtime validation.
findings.recommended_fix: Type apiCall<Todo[]>; validate responses; enable strict; remove the ignore flags.

findings.title: id type disagrees across backend, frontend and documentation
evidence: Runtime: backend returns an integer id
Frontend declares id: string; docs declare a UUID string
NO live bug today - both sides of todo.id === id are numbers at runtime
findings.impact: Types are wrong; passing an id from a URL param (a string) would make the strict comparison silently fail.
findings.recommended_fix: Align the TypeScript type to number; correct the documentation.

findings.title: Dead code and unused configuration throughout

ruff: 14 unused imports, 5 unused variables

VERIFIED: the file is an empty SQLite database with zero tables - no data exposure
findings.impact: Repository hygiene only. Commit 6720579 claims to have removed it; it did not.

A live ES cluster UUID, node id, Kibana alert-rule document ids and internal index names are pasted
The operator's workstation LAN IP 10.20.30.117 appears in an alert table

findings.impact: GET /api/v1/todos/stats would 422 rather than 404. Cosmetic.
